title: Settlement Fails Playbook
body:
Settlement Fails Playbook
Owner: Ravi Patel, Head of Operations
Last updated: 2026-07-14
Applies to: Operations (Settlements, Payments, Wire Room), Trading, Risk, Compliance

Purpose
This playbook describes how Halcyon Ridge Capital identifies, triages, escalates, and resolves failed settlements. A fail is any trade that does not settle on its contractual settlement date because of missing securities, missing cash, instruction mismatch, or a counterparty or custodian issue. The goal is to cut aged fails, limit financing and buy-in costs, and keep Trading, Risk, and Finance informed early.

Systems Involved
SettlementEngine is the system of record for trade settlement and clearing. All fails are tracked there as exceptions with a status, reason code, and age in business days. PaymentsGateway handles ACH and wire cash movements, and is the route for cash funding of fails and for claims and compensation payments. SettlementEngine depends on OMS and GLCore, so a fail can originate from an upstream order or ledger problem as well as from the counterparty. Before escalating externally, always confirm that OMS trade details and GLCore postings are correct.

Daily Fails Routine
1. By 07:30 ET the Settlements Specialist on shift pulls the overnight exceptions report from SettlementEngine and tags every item with a reason code: SHORT (securities not delivered), CASH (funding shortfall), MISMATCH (instruction or SSI discrepancy), CPTY (counterparty or custodian hold), or INTERNAL (booking or allocation error).
2. By 08:15 ET the settlements lead posts the fails summary in #recon with counts by reason code, aggregate notional, and any item aged three business days or more.
3. Items tagged INTERNAL are routed immediately to the owning desk. Trading must confirm or amend allocations in OMS by 09:30 ET.
4. Items tagged MISMATCH are re-confirmed with the counterparty and the instruction is corrected and resubmitted the same morning.
5. By 14:00 ET the team reviews all open items against the cut-offs of the custodians and clearing agents so that remaining fixes can still land for same-day settlement.

Cash Funding and Wire Handling
When a fail is caused by a cash shortfall, the Settlements Specialist requests funding through the Payments team. Any wire release goes through PaymentsGateway and is processed by the Wire Room under standard dual approval. No one may release a payment they initiated. The Wire Room console shows the status, but the payment record in PaymentsGateway is authoritative. If a payment is held by fraud scoring, do not work around the hold. Contact Compliance in #compliance and wait for clearance.

Escalation Thresholds
Age one business day: Settlements owns the item and contacts the counterparty operations desk.
Age three business days: Escalate to the Head of Operations and notify the responsible Trading desk head. Trading must provide a view on whether to cancel and rebook, borrow securities, or wait.
Age five business days, or any single fail above $5M notional: Notify Risk, specifically the Market Risk Manager, who assesses exposure and capital impact. Finance is copied so that financing charges can be accrued in GLCore.
Any fail exposed to a mandatory buy-in: Escalate the same day to the Head of Operations and the Chief Operating Officer. Trading decides on action before the buy-in notice deadline.

Resolution Options
Partial settlement where the counterparty and custodian permit it, which reduces exposure quickly.
Securities borrow or a sourced delivery through the Trading desk.
Cancel and rebook for genuine booking errors, only with Trading and Compliance agreement where the change affects a reportable record.
Claims and compensation for costs caused by the counterparty, documented in SettlementEngine and paid or received through PaymentsGateway.

Incident Handling
If more than ten fails share a common cause, such as a SettlementEngine outage or a stale feed from OMS, treat it as an operational incident. Open a thread in #incidents, name an incident lead from Operations, and notify Technology through #it-ops. Settlements must keep a manual log of affected trades until the system is confirmed healthy. Note that ReconLegacy, the legacy end-of-day reconciliation batch, will show breaks for fails. Do not clear these breaks manually until the underlying fail is resolved or formally written off.

Documentation and Reporting
Every fail needs a note in SettlementEngine with the reason code, counterparty contact, actions taken, and expected settlement date. The weekly fails report goes to the Chief Operating Officer and the Head of Risk every Monday and includes aging buckets, repeat counterparties, and total financing cost. Counterparties that cause repeated fails are reviewed monthly with Trading and Risk.

Questions
Post in #recon or contact Ravi Patel directly. This playbook is reviewed each quarter and after any significant fail event.
